                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.

         1       Libous, legislative resolution paying just

         2       tribute and remembering the 13 victims who

         3       lost their lives to a gunman during the

         4       American Civic Association tragedy on Friday,

         5       April 3, 2009.

         6                  "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body

         7       recognizes the tragic incident that took place

         8       at the American Civic Association in

         9       Binghamton, New York, and the loss of life

        10       that has been sustained by the victims as well

        11       as the heartache and suffering of their loved

        12       ones; and

        13                  "WHEREAS, 13 people, comprised of

        14       two employees and 11 immigrants who were

        15       inside the upstate New York immigration

        16       center, were shot and killed by a single

        17       gunman on Friday April 3, 2009; and

        18                  "WHEREAS, The community center was

        19       used in great part to teach people from

        20       countries as far away as Kazakhstan and

        21       Uzbekistan to speak and write English, with

        22       the goal of gaining U.S. citizenship; and

        23                  "WHEREAS, The deceased include

        24       Parveen Nin Ali, Binghamton, New York; Dolores



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3709



         1       Yigal, Binghamton, New York; Marc Henry

         2       Bernard, Endicott, New York; Maria Sonia

         3       Bernard, Endicott, New York; Li Guo,

         4       Binghamton, New York; Hong Xiu Mao, Greene,

         5       New York; Lan Ho, Binghamton, New York; Hai

         6       Hong Zhong, Endwell, New York; Maria Zobniw,

         7       Binghamton, New York; Roberta "Bobbie" King,

         8       Binghamton, New York; Almir O. Alves; Jiang

         9       Ling, Endicott, New York; and Layla Khalil,

        10       Binghamton, New York; and

        11                  "WHEREAS, This Legislative Body is

        12       moved with great respect and reverent esteem

        13       to pay tribute to the heroic actions of each

        14       and every victim, knowing that their memory

        15       will forever remain with their families; and

        16                  "WHEREAS, Armed with a humanistic

        17       spirit, imbued with a sense of compassion, and

        18       comforted by loving families, each of these

        19       13 brave individuals leaves behind a legacy

        20       which will long endure the passage of time and

        21       will remain as a comforting memory to all they

        22       befriended; now, therefore, be it

        23                  "RESOLVED, That this Legislative

        24       Body pause in its deliberations to pay just



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3710



         1       tribute to the 13 victims who lost their lives

         2       as the result of the senseless action of a

         3       gunman during the American Civic Association

         4       tragedy, and to express sincere condolences to

         5       their families and the Binghamton community;

         6       and be it further

         7                  "RESOLVED, That copies of this

         8       resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted

         9       to the families of the 13 victims."

        10                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:

        11       Senator Libous.

        12                  SENATOR LIBOUS:    Thank you,

        13       Mr. President.

        14                  Mr. President, on April 3rd we were

        15       all in this chamber debating budget bills, and

        16       I got a call from the Governor, who shared

        17       with me about the senseless killings that were

        18       taking place in Binghamton at the time we were

        19       in this chamber debating budget bills.

        20                  At that time he had not known the

        21       severity of injuries or if anyone had lost

        22       their life, but he told that there was a

        23       gunman and that they believed that at that

        24       time four people were killed.



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3711



         1                  Shortly thereafter, this house was

         2       extremely gracious, under Senator Smith's

         3       leadership, and allowed me to vote, and the

         4       Governor and Senator Smith arranged for

         5       transportation for me to go back to

         6       Binghamton.

         7                  Mr. President, there were

         8       13 victims.  Eleven immigrants were killed,

         9       men and women who came to this country for an

        10       opportunity.  They were taking a class in

        11       English.  They were learning how to speak

        12       English so that they could contribute to this

        13       country, our society, in the right way, in the

        14       way that it's supposed to be done, not

        15       illegally, but to become very proud legal

        16       American citizens.

        17                  They were gunned down in the

        18       English class.  It was a horrific sight,

        19       Mr. President.  It was tragic, horrific,

        20       shocking.  You can't put into words what took

        21       place that day.

        22                  Two other victims were employees.

        23       Roberta "Bobbie" King, a well-established

        24       teacher in the Binghamton School District who



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3712



         1       volunteered and taught English classes at the

         2       American Civic Association where the tragedy

         3       took place, was killed in the classroom.

         4       Another woman, Maria Zobniw, a worker who

         5       wasn't supposed to work that day -- a very

         6       proud member of the Ukrainian community, an

         7       active worker, volunteer, participant at the

         8       American Civic Association -- was also killed.

         9                  All heroes, in my estimation, all

        10       the men and women, the two workers who wanted

        11       to help others get a better life.  Certainly

        12       those who lost their lives in this tragedy

        13       wanted to become what we all are, as American

        14       citizens.  They wanted a piece of the American

        15       dream just like we've been able to share.

        16                  Mr. President, the American Civic

        17       Association has for many, many years -- I

        18       believe since 1939, and I may be off a few

        19       years -- been the place in the Binghamton

        20       area, the Triple Cities, where men and women

        21       could come from another country -- like my

        22       grandparents, who came from Lebanon, used the

        23       services of the American Civic Association,

        24       like thousands of others -- an organization



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3713



         1       that helped people to share and become part of

         2       that American dream.

         3                  Our community was shocked that day

         4       and is still stunned.  Binghamton, New York,

         5       is a small town in upstate New York.  It's a

         6       wonderful place to live.  I was born and

         7       raised in the area, certainly lived in the

         8       city for many, many years.  My grandfather,

         9       when he came to this country, opened up a

        10       business, a grocery store, and it fed our

        11       families for over fifty years.

        12                  It's a community that didn't expect

        13       anything like this.  And I'm sure that there

        14       are no communities in our great country that

        15       ever expect anything like this.

        16                  We have come together, the response

        17       from the community, and certainly the men and

        18       women and public officials, from the Governor

        19       on down, and the charities that came to help,

        20       everybody has come together to mourn and to

        21       try to get through this tragedy.  Our goal is

        22       to make sure that the American Civic

        23       Association can again be that beacon that will

        24       open the door for those who choose to come to



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3714



         1       this country and to get a little bit of that

         2       American dream.

         3                  When I went back home and tried to

         4       do whatever little I could do to help, on

         5       Sunday -- the tragedy took place on a Friday.

         6       On Sunday, there was a vigil mass.  Several

         7       thousand people attended.  And it didn't

         8       really hit me until I saw the members of the

         9       families -- from all difficult religious

        10       denominations, different countries, ethnic

        11       backgrounds -- and I saw the children, the two

        12       young kids who lost their mother and father.

        13       That's when it really hit me.  It hit me as to

        14       what happens for them next.  How do we take

        15       care of them, how do we provide for them, how

        16       do we give them that opportunity for the dream

        17       that their mother and father or their loved

        18       ones wanted?

        19                  And that's what our goal is,

        20       Mr. President and members of this body.  The

        21       goal of our community is to try and make sure

        22       that the family members do experience that

        23       American dream to become citizens of this

        24       country, to be able to enjoy this land, so



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3715



         1       that the lives that were lost were not lost in

         2       vain, that there was a purpose and there was a

         3       real serious purpose.

         4                  So, Mr. President, I stand before

         5       this body today with a very heavy heart for

         6       the family members and certainly the two

         7       workers who lost their lives on this very

         8       tragic day in Binghamton.

        16       116, by Senator Onorato, Senate Print 3357, an

        17       act to amend the Labor Law.

        18                  SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:

        19       Explanation.

        20                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:

        21       Senator Onorato, an explanation has been

        22       requested by Senator DeFrancisco.

        23                  SENATOR ONORATO:    Mr. President,

        24       this would require employers to give written



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3720



         1       consent, notice to the rate of pay and the

         2       regular payday upon hiring, and get written

         3       acknowledgment thereof from each of the

         4       employees.

         5                  This bill would allow workers to

         6       know whether their paychecks properly show the

         7       regular and overtime hourly wages that their

         8       employers agreed to at the time of hiring.

         9                  Many workers are paid on a weekly

        10       basis.  They receive a paycheck showing a lump

        11       sum for wages for their regular and overtime

        12       work.  This makes it difficult to know what

        13       their overtime rate of pay is and whether

        14       their employer has properly included overtime

        15       in the paycheck.

        16                  The current law does not go far

        17       enough to many employees, since employers can

        18       just give verbal notice of the hourly rates at

        19       the time of hiring.  If the employee

        20       understands the wage rates to which they are

        21       entitled, it will help prevent confusion

        22       between an employer and employee regarding

        23       overtime pay.

        24                  This bill was introduced by the



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3721



         1       Department of Labor because of widespread

         2       violations throughout New York regarding

         3       underpayment of regular and overtime wages to

         4       workers.  The bill will help the Commissioner

         5       of Labor to better enforce the wage laws and

         6       properly compute the overtime rate to which

         7       the employee is entitled.

         8                  And I believe this bill was past

         9       last year by the Assembly unanimously.

        10                  SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:    Would

        11       Senator Onorato respond to a couple of

        12       questions, please.

        14       Senator Onorato, do you yield?

        23                  SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:    Would

        24       Senator Onorato respond to another question?

         1       rate of any overtime pay?

         2                  SENATOR ONORATO:    It is.

         3                  SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:    Thank you,

         4       Senator Onorato.

         5                  On the bill.

         6                  ACTING PRESIDENT VALESKY:

         7       Senator DeFrancisco, on the bill.

         8                  SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:    You know,

         9       we have just gone through a budget process

        10       which raised taxes on so many things and made

        11       New York State even more inhospitable to

        12       business.

        13                  I periodically voted against many

        14       of the notice bills where you have to post

        15       some kind of notice for this or post some kind

        16       of notice for that, because in many instances

        17       I believe it's just another onerous burden

        18       placed upon people -- usually businesses in

        19       this state -- that really is just an

        20       unnecessary expense.  And I've opposed

        21       Republican bills as well along the same line.

        22                  We're now one of the least, I

        23       think -- according to some groups, the second

        24       least favorable state for business to operate



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3724



         1       in.  We're surpassed only by California.

         2                  Right now the law requires

         3       individuals to be notified of their rate of

         4       pay, notified of the overtime pay.  They get a

         5       pay stub which indicates their pay rate and

         6       what pay they got.

         7                  The Department of Labor is also

         8       allowed, under current law, to make any

         9       inquiries they choose to make with respect to

        10       an employment situation as to whether overtime

        11       pay is being used.

        12                  To require an acknowledgment from

        13       an employee in writing seems to me just

        14       another piece of paper that has so little

        15       importance.  And whatever importance it might

        16       have or benefit it might have is clearly

        17       outweighed by another needless requirement of

        18       employers in the State of New York.

        19                  If this was a school district, we'd

        20       call it an unfunded mandate.  What it

        21       basically is is another cost to business which

        22       either raises the product or ends up requiring

        23       the employer to cut somewhere else.  And it

        24       may be that very employee or one of those very



                      Candyco Transcription Service, Inc.
                                (518) 371-8910
                                                         3725



         1       employees' jobs who now really doesn't need an

         2       acknowledgment to be produced and provided,

         3       doesn't really need anything in writing that

         4       isn't already provided through the pay stub.

         5                  And it just seems to me that this

         6       is a bill that just adds to the cost of

         7       business and will hasten our steps towards

         8       being the least hospitable state for business

         9       in this union.  And that doesn't bode well for

        10       employees.  And employees is who we want.  We
